name: Rishikesh
description: Nestled in the Himalayan foothills along the holy Ganges, Rishikesh is renowned as the Yoga Capital of the World and a prime adventure hub for white-water rafting, camping, and bungee jumping.
travel_tips: Book river rafting with certified guides only.
Attend the sunset Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat early for good seats.
Alcohol and non-vegetarian food are strictly prohibited in the holy zone.
best_season: September to November, March to May

name: Goa (North & South)
description: A coastal paradise famous for sun-kissed Arabian Sea beaches, vibrant nightlife, Portuguese colonial architecture, fresh seafood, and tranquil spice plantations.
travel_tips: Renting a scooter (₹350-₹500/day) is the most economical way to travel.
South Goa offers serene beaches, while North Goa is bustling with clubs and markets.
Carry cash for beach shacks as card networks can be spotty.

name: Manali
description: High-altitude Himalayan resort town on the Beas River, gateway to Solang Valley, Rohtang Pass, and tranquil apple orchards surrounded by snow-capped peaks.
travel_tips: Obtain Rohtang Pass permits in advance online.
Stay in Old Manali for bohemian cafes and quiet pine forests.
Winter visits require warm thermal layers and waterproof boots.

name: Jaipur
description: The regal Pink City of Rajasthan, steeped in Rajput history, majestic hill fortresses, vibrant bazaars, and opulent royal palaces.
travel_tips: Buy a composite monument ticket to save on admission fees.
Try authentic Dal Baati Churma and Pyaaz Kachori near Johari Bazaar.
E-rickshaws and Jaipur Metro provide cheap inner-city commute.

name: Varanasi
description: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities on the banks of the sacred River Ganga, celebrated for its ancient spiritual ghats, silk weaving, and labyrinthine alleys.
travel_tips: Negotiate morning hand-rowed boat rides at the ghats beforehand (₹300-₹500).
Explore narrow gallis on foot to find famous street food like Malaiyo and Banarasi Paan.
Dress modestly when visiting temple sanctums.

name: Munnar
description: Rolling hills blanketed with emerald green tea plantations, misty valleys, colonial bungalows, and refreshing mountain waterfalls in God's Own Country.
travel_tips: Book Eravikulam National Park safari tickets online to skip queues.
Hire an auto-rickshaw for scenic half-day circuit tours.
Sample fresh spices and artisanal homemade chocolates at local markets.

name: Hampi
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with an otherworldly boulder-strewn landscape sheltering the spectacular ruins of the 14th-century Vijayanagara Empire.
travel_tips: Rent a bicycle (₹150/day) or moped to traverse the sprawling ruins.
Climb Matanga Hill early morning for an unforgettable 360-degree sunrise panorama.
Respect sacred active worship areas across temple compounds.

name: Udaipur
description: Known as the City of Lakes and Venice of the East, famed for its shimmering Lake Pichola, fairy-tale marble palaces, and scenic Aravalli hills.
travel_tips: Catch the evening folk dance performance at Bagore Ki Haveli.
Lakeside rooftop restaurants offer stunning views of lit palaces at dusk.
Walking through the old city alleys is faster than hailing large cabs.

name: Gokarna
description: A tranquil coastal pilgrimage haven with pristine crescent beaches bordered by rocky cliffs, offering a peaceful, soulful alternative to commercial beach resorts.
travel_tips: The 5-beach cliff trek is best done in the early morning.
Stay in rustic beachside huts or cottages along Kudle Beach.
Temple dress codes apply when entering the sanctum of Mahabaleshwar Temple.

name: Amritsar
description: The spiritual and cultural center of the Sikh community, home to the resplendent Golden Temple, poignant colonial history, and world-renowned Punjabi culinary delights.
travel_tips: Cover your head and remove footwear inside the Golden Temple complex.
Partake in the Langar (community kitchen) for an inspiring egalitarian feast.
Reach Wagah border by 3:30 PM to secure bleacher seats for the ceremony.

name: Darjeeling
description: Queen of the Hills set against the breathtaking backdrop of Mount Kanchenjunga, world-famous for its aromatic orthodox tea estates and historic UNESCO Toy Train.
travel_tips: Start at 3:30 AM for the Tiger Hill sunrise to avoid traffic bottlenecks.
Book your DHR Toy Train ride well in advance during peak season.
Sip authentic first-flush Darjeeling tea at historic Mall Road cafes.
best_season: March to May, October to December

name: Pondicherry (Puducherry)
description: A charming French colonial coastal enclave featuring pastel-hued mustard villas, tree-lined boulevards, peaceful beaches, chic cafes, and the experimental township of Auroville.
travel_tips: Rent a bicycle or retro scooter to leisurely explore French Quarter.
Visit Matrimandir viewing point; interior meditation passes require advance booking.
Enjoy French-Tamil fusion cuisine and artisanal bakeries on Rue Suffren.

name: Leh-Ladakh
description: The Land of High Mountain Passes, distinguished by dramatic stark cold-desert landscapes, cobalt blue glacial lakes, Tibetan Buddhist gompas, and world's highest motorable roads.
travel_tips: Mandatory 48-hour acclimatization in Leh before ascending higher passes.
Carry valid photo ID and obtain Inner Line Permits (ILP) for restricted zones.
Stay hydrated with garlic soup and avoid overexertion during initial days.

name: Jim Corbett National Park
description: India's oldest national park nestled along the Ramganga River, world-famous for its thriving Royal Bengal Tiger population, elephant herds, and dense sal forests.
travel_tips: Book official safari permits 45-90 days in advance via forest department portal.
Morning safaris offer the best odds for wildlife spotting and birding.
Stay inside Dhikala forest rest house for an authentic wilderness immersion.

name: Varkala
description: A stunning seaside cliff haven overlooking the Arabian Sea, featuring dramatic red sandstone promontories, tranquil beach shacks, natural springs, and bohemian yoga retreats.
travel_tips: Papanasam beach waters are believed to wash away sins and have healing mineral springs.
Cliff-edge restaurants offer fresh catches of the day and spectacular sunsets.
Varkala Railway Station connects directly to Trivandrum and Kochi.

name: Khajuraho
description: UNESCO World Heritage marvel built by the Chandela dynasty, famed for its masterfully carved medieval Hindu and Jain temples depicting cosmic life, spirituality, and artistic brilliance.
travel_tips: Hire an official ASI licensed guide to truly appreciate temple iconography.
Visit Raneh Falls (30 mins drive) for pure crystalline granite rock canyons.
Evenings host the mesmerizing light and sound narration on temple grounds.

name: Bir Billing
description: World-famous paragliding capital nestled in the Kangra Valley, renowned for exhilarating tandem flights, Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, and laid-back tea gardens.
travel_tips: Paragliding costs approx ₹2,500-₹3,500 per flight including GoPro recording.
Check weather windows; paragliding halts during high winds or rain.
Bir colony has great eco-cafes serving Tibetan momos and herbal mountain teas.

name: Dharamshala & McLeod Ganj
description: Perched against the mighty Dhauladhar mountain range, the seat of the Dalai Lama and Tibetan Government-in-Exile, blending Tibetan spirituality, pine forests, and high-altitude hiking.
travel_tips: The Triund trek is a 4-hour moderate hike with jaw-dropping views of Dhauladhar peaks.
Try authentic Thukpa, Tingmo, and Apple Crumble on Temple Road.
HPCA stadium is one of the highest altitude cricket grounds in the world.

name: Jodhpur
description: The majestic Blue City commanded by the invincible Mehrangarh Fort rising sheer above indigo-painted Brahmin cubical houses at the edge of the Thar Desert.
travel_tips: The audio tour at Mehrangarh Fort is among the most informative in India.
Don't miss the famous Mirchi Bada and Shahi Samosa near the Clock Tower.
Head up to rooftop restaurants in Navchokiya to capture the sea of blue homes.

name: Spiti Valley
description: The Middle Land between Tibet and India—a remote Trans-Himalayan wonderland with centuries-old monasteries clinging to cliffs, moonscapes, and sparkling starry skies.
travel_tips: Post a postcard from Hikkim to yourself or friends.
Travel with local experienced 4x4 drivers due to rugged river crossings.
Very limited ATM availability and mobile network (only BSNL/Jio in spots).

name: Ooty & Nilgiris
description: The Queen of Hill Stations in the Blue Nilgiri Mountains, famed for eucalyptus groves, tea gardens, botanical gardens, and the scenic Nilgiri Mountain Railway.
travel_tips: Book the toy train journey between Mettupalayam, Coonoor, and Ooty on IRCTC.
Avalanche Lake requires an eco-tourism forest vehicle pass.
Sample homemade dark truffles and eucalyptus oils at the local market.

name: Puri
description: One of India's Char Dham holy pilgrimage cities situated on the Bay of Bengal, home to the sacred Jagannath Temple, golden surf beaches, and the nearby Konark Sun Temple.
travel_tips: Only practicing Hindus are allowed inside Jagannath Temple sanctum.
Visit Blue Flag Golden Beach for clean, well-guarded waters.
Buy authentic hand-painted palm-leaf scrolls directly from Raghurajpur artisans.

name: Lucknow
description: The historic City of Nawabs along the Gomti River, internationally celebrated for its refined etiquette, grand Mughal-Awadhi architecture, Chikankari embroidery, and legendary kebabs.
travel_tips: Hire an authorized guide to navigate the labyrinth of Bhool Bhulaiya without getting lost.
Taste original Galouti kebabs at Chowk and Prakash Kulfi at Aminabad.
Shop for authentic hand-embroidered Chikankari kurtas in Janpath.

name: Gangtok
description: A clean, vibrant Himalayan capital city offering mesmerizing views of Mt. Kanchenjunga, vibrant Buddhist monasteries, alpine cable cars, and rhododendron sanctuaries.
travel_tips: Nathula Pass and Tsomgo Lake require permits arranged a day in advance via registered travel agents.
MG Marg is completely pedestrian and litter-free with charming cafes.
Sikkim is a 100% organic state; relish locally grown organic meals.
best_season: March to May, October to mid-December

name: Kaziranga National Park
description: A UNESCO World Heritage sanctuary along the mighty Brahmaputra floodplain, sheltering two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceroses and rich birdlife.
attractions: Kaziranga National Orchid and Biodiversity Park
travel_tips: Book the early morning elephant safari for close-up views of rhinos in the elephant grass.
Visit the Orchid Park to witness traditional Bihu dance performances.
The park remains closed during the monsoon season (June to September).

name: Kochi (Cochin)
description: Historic Malabar port city blending Chinese fishing nets, Dutch palaces, Portuguese churches, spice trade markets, and a flourishing modern art biennale.
attractions: Fort Kochi Beach & Iconic Chinese Fishing Nets
travel_tips: Hop on the Kochi Water Metro for an ultra-cheap, air-conditioned scenic harbor cruise.
Jew Town is ideal for antique spice boxes, hand-woven cotton, and curio shopping.
Watch a live Kathakali dance makeup and storytelling session at dusk.

name: Auli
description: Premier Himalayan ski resort perched at 3,000 meters, famous for gentle powdery ski slopes, sweeping views of Nanda Devi peak, and the longest cable car in Asia.
travel_tips: Skiing season peaks from January to early March.
Take the 4-km scenic ropeway from Joshimath instead of driving up hairpin turns in snow.
Carry sunscreen and UV-protective sunglasses to shield against high-altitude snow glare.
best_season: December to March for snow; April to June for lush meadows

name: Shillong & Cherrapunji
description: The Scotland of the East in the Abode of Clouds, blessed with rolling pine-clad hills, cascading plunge waterfalls, limestone caves, and ancient bio-engineered living root bridges.
attractions: Double Decker Living Root Bridge at Nongriat
travel_tips: The hike to Double Decker Living Root Bridge involves 3,500 stairs each way; start early and carry a bamboo stick.
Dawki boating is best in winter (Dec-Feb) when water is glass-transparent.
Try local Khasi pork dishes (Jadoh) in Police Bazar.

name: Agra
description: Home to the immortal Taj Mahal on the Yamuna riverbank, an architectural pinnacle of the Mughal Empire featuring grand red sandstone forts and tombs.
travel_tips: Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays for prayers.
Visit at sunrise to avoid the midday crowd and oppressive heat.
Sample famous Petha sweets from Panchhi Petha stores.

name: Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep)
description: A pristine tropical island in the Bay of Bengal boasting world-class turquoise waters, powdery white sand beaches, dense rainforests, and rich coral reefs.
travel_tips: Government and private catamarans (Makruzz/Green Ocean) connect Port Blair to Havelock.
Pre-book scuba diving with PADI-certified dive shops.
Carry sufficient cash as island internet can disrupt digital payments.

name: Tirthan Valley
description: An unspoiled, tranquil eco-tourism paradise at the gateway to the UNESCO Great Himalayan National Park, renowned for pristine trout streams, deodar forests, and rustic wooden hamlets.
travel_tips: A fishing permit from the local fisheries office is required for angling.
Serolsar lake trek from Jalori Pass is 5 km through scenic oak and rhododendron forests.
Homestays provide delicious Himachali Siddu and walnut chutney.
best_season: March to June, October to November

name: Bhopal & Sanchi
description: The City of Lakes combining heritage nawabi mosques and massive man-made lakes with easy access to the UNESCO Sanchi Great Buddhist Stupa and prehistoric Bhimbetka rock shelters.
travel_tips: Bhimbetka and Sanchi make rewarding half-day trips from Bhopal.
Enjoy peaceful boat cruises on the Upper Lake at sunset.
Try Bhopal's distinct Poha-Jalebi and Sulemani Chai in old city chowks.

name: Ziro Valley
description: An idyllic emerald pine plateau inhabited by the indigenous Apatani tribe, famed for sophisticated wet-rice fish farming, traditional village crafts, and the outdoor Ziro Music Festival.
travel_tips: Domestic visitors require an Inner Line Permit (ILP); foreign visitors need a Protected Area Permit (PAP).
Respect tribal village culture; always ask before photographing community elders.
September is lively with the renowned open-air Ziro Music Festival.

name: Kolkata
description: The Cultural Capital of India on the Hooghly River, renowned for its grand British colonial architecture, literary heritage, historic yellow cabs, trams, and irresistible Bengali sweets.
attractions: College Street Boi Para & Coffee House
travel_tips: Ride India's oldest operating tramway for a nostalgic city transit experience.
Indulge in Kathi rolls on Park Street, Mishti Doi, and freshly made Rosogollas.
The Kolkata Metro is swift, clean, and connects major tourist sectors.

name: Hyderabad
description: The City of Pearls and Nizams, where 400-year-old minarets and colossal rock forts harmoniously coexist with cutting-edge IT campuses and legendary Hyderabadi Dum Biryani.
travel_tips: Savor authentic mutton dum biryani and Irani chai paired with Osmania biscuits.
Visit Golconda Fort late afternoon to stay for the evocative sunset sound-and-light show.
Hyderabad Metro provides fast connectivity across the twin cities.
